- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per period unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model overreacts to auction supply — reduce forecast sensitivity to supply net by 15–20%.
- When sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model often fails to adjust — apply mean reversion to forecast 3–5 periods ahead.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if recent 18-day history shows volatility >15% range, model tends to smooth too much — allow 3–5% volatility buffer in forecast spread.
